newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Euro-MPs to demand ban on cloning.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs to demand ban on cloning.

text.p: The European Parliament, reacting to the successful cloning of a sheep at Scotland's Roslin Institute, is expected next week to call for a ban on the cloning of humans and a ban or moratorium on the cloning of animals.

The parliament will also demand a statement from the European Commission saying how it intends to approach this sensitive subject, especially as far as European Union funding for research into genetic engineering is concerned.
Green MEPs are expected to take the lead in demanding an immediate end to all EU and private funding for research into human and animal cloning techniques.

A spokesman for the Socialists, the largest political group in the parliament, said his party wanted the EU to ban human cloning now and take a lead in reaching a binding international agreement to this effect.
As far back as 1993, the parliament demanded an end to all human cloning after American scientist Dr Jerry Hall announced he had succeeded in creating identical twins in vitro.
The Socialists had still not finalised their position on animal cloning, the spokesman said.
Advocates of this technique say it would make it possible, for example, to produce sheep which are entirely free from scrapie, a disease similar to mad cow disease.
Opponents warn that cloning could have the effect of narrowing the genetic diversity of livestock. It could also lead to the physical and mental disorders associated with excessive in-breeding.
Green Euro-MPs tend to support the latter view and are expected next week to demand an outright ban on animal cloning.

A draft resolution from the Greens warns that animal cloning would encourage the industrialisation of farming and undermine attempts to reorient the EU's common agriculture policy towards sustainable practices.

Euro-MPs are also due to call for the creation of an international body to examine the ethical considerations raised by cloning and the implications of the technique for health and for the competitivity of industry and farming.
